fields.sections.0.h: Background and Intent of the Urgent Announcement
fields.sections.1.h: Declaration of AI Exclusion and Pure Human Work
fields.sections.2.h: Original Plans and Rapidly Changing Timeline
fields.sections.4.h: Requests to the Academic Community and Hope
fields.sections.0.ko: Even while busy attending a meeting of American Mathematical Society officers, the author is urgently announcing this news. He emphasizes that Alessandro Mazzulo has presented a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), and that renowned mathematician Brian Conrad has reviewed it precisely over several months and provided feedback. The current assessment suggests the proof appears sound.
fields.sections.1.ko: The author explicitly states that this proof is "all human work with no AI." In a situation where skepticism about AI tool use exists in the modern mathematics community, by preemptively declaring that the work was accomplished through pure human thinking alone, an intent to emphasize the authenticity of the proof becomes evident.
fields.sections.2.ko: The original plan was to invite Mazzulo to Stanford and refine the paper over one year before releasing it after sufficient verification. However, based on current circumstances, the decision was made that releasing this draft earlier is best. This can be interpreted as a strategy to quickly inform the academic community of the discovery's importance while simultaneously conducting broad verification in parallel.
fields.sections.3.ko: The author has deep trust in Conrad's judgment and repeatedly emphasizes that he invested considerable time and thought in carefully reviewing Mazzulo's work. This suggests that more than mere formal review was conducted—expert-level in-depth review in the field of algebraic geometry took place.
fields.sections.4.ko: The author appeals to the mathematics community to quickly review the draft, formalize the proof, and fill any small gaps that may be discovered. Finally, the expression "I really hope this works" reveals a sincere wish for this proof to succeed.
fields.caveat: This text is at an early stage of proof announcement and has not yet undergone broad peer review by the international mathematics community, so it is difficult to confirm whether the proof succeeds until final verification is completed.
